name: Data Visualization
description: Choosing and building clear, honest and accessible charts that reveal patterns in data.

questions.question: Which chart type is usually best for showing how monthly revenue changes over two years?
options: Pie chart
Scatter plot matrix
Line chart
Treemap
questions.explanation: Line charts connect values along a continuous time axis, making trends and seasonality easy to see.

questions.question: Which chart best shows the distribution of a single continuous variable such as delivery times?
options: Histogram
Pie chart
Stacked bar chart of categories
Gauge chart
questions.explanation: A histogram bins a continuous variable and shows its shape, center, spread and skew.

questions.question: Why should the value axis of a bar chart normally start at zero?
options: Charting libraries cannot render other starting values
It makes the chart load faster
Zero is required for colorblind accessibility
Bar length encodes the value, so a truncated axis exaggerates differences between bars
questions.explanation: Readers compare bar lengths; starting above zero distorts the ratios between them and can mislead.

questions.question: Which practice best makes a chart accessible to readers with color vision deficiency?
options: Use red and green as the only way to distinguish series
Use a colorblind-safe palette and add redundant encoding such as direct labels, markers or patterns
Use as many bright colors as possible
Remove the legend to reduce clutter
questions.explanation: Red-green encoding is a common failure; palettes designed for CVD plus non-color cues ensure everyone can read the chart.

questions.question: A scatter plot of 200,000 points is a solid blob due to overplotting. What is the best fix?
options: Convert it to a pie chart
Use a 3D bar chart
Use transparency (alpha), a hexbin plot or a 2D density plot to reveal where points concentrate
Randomly delete outliers until the blob disappears
questions.explanation: Alpha blending, hexagonal binning or density contours show point concentration that overlapping opaque markers hide.

questions.question: You need readers to compare the market share of 12 companies precisely. Which visualization is most effective?
options: A pie chart with 12 slices
A donut chart with a legend
A 3D exploded pie chart
A horizontal bar chart sorted by share
questions.explanation: People judge aligned lengths far more accurately than angles or areas; sorting further eases ranking and comparison.

practical.title: Plot a revenue trend
practical.instructions: A pandas DataFrame df has columns 'month' and 'revenue'. Write Python code (matplotlib, pandas plotting, seaborn or plotly) that draws a line chart of revenue by month with a chart title and labeled x and y axes.
practical.expected_output: import matplotlib.pyplot as plt; plt.plot(df['month'], df['revenue']); plt.title('Monthly Revenue'); plt.xlabel('Month'); plt.ylabel('Revenue'); plt.show()

rubric.hint: Use plt.plot(), df.plot(kind='line'), sns.lineplot() or px.line().

rubric.description: Uses the month and revenue columns
rubric.hint: Plot 'month' on the x-axis and 'revenue' on the y-axis.
Add a title with plt.title(), ax.set_title() or title=.
Label axes with plt.xlabel()/plt.ylabel() or ax.set_xlabel()/ax.set_ylabel().

tasks.title: Learn to choose the right chart
tasks.description: Explore From Data to Viz and its decision tree for choosing charts by data type. Summarize when to use line, bar, histogram, scatter and box plots, and common caveats.
tasks.completion_criteria: A one-page chart selection cheat sheet with one example and one pitfall per chart type.

tasks.title: Make basic charts with matplotlib
tasks.description: Using a small data set, create a line chart, bar chart, histogram and scatter plot with matplotlib, each with a title, axis labels and units.
tasks.completion_criteria: Four saved chart images, each with a title and labeled axes.

tasks.title: Explore a data set with seaborn
tasks.description: Follow the seaborn tutorial and perform exploratory analysis on a public data set using distribution, relational and categorical plots, using a colorblind-safe palette.
tasks.completion_criteria: A notebook with at least six plots and a written insight beneath each.

tasks.title: Redesign a misleading chart and publish a visual report
tasks.description: Find a poorly designed chart, critique it (axes, encoding, color, clutter), and redesign it. Then produce a short visual report of 4-6 charts on a data set of your choice answering a clear question.
tasks.completion_criteria: A before/after critique plus a report whose charts each have a takeaway title, labeled axes, source note and accessible colors.
